El Salvador has launched a military operation to rescue four aviation technicians from a UN-backed security force whom Haitian gangs are holding hostage. President Nayib Bukele said the men must be returned unharmed after they disappeared on Sunday when armed gangs ambushed their vehicle outside Port-au-Prince. The vehicle caught fire, forcing its occupants to flee. Bukele said the Salvadorans were pilots and technical personnel responsible for medical evacuations rather than combat operations. He warned gang leaders of further consequences unless all four were released alive. Fighting during rescue efforts has already injured four members of the international force. ... UN projections now put global warming at 2.6C above pre-industrial levels by 2100 even if countries fulfil their climate pledges, up from last year’s forecast. The UN Environment Programme says exceeding the Paris Agreement’s 1.5C limit is now unavoidable, with current policies pointing to 2.8C of warming. ... The report attributes the deteriorating outlook partly to the United States’ withdrawal from the Paris Agreement and rising American emissions. US emissions increased by 133 million tonnes of CO2 equivalent in 2025, driven by electricity demand and renewed coal generation. Global emissions remained broadly unchanged at 58.4 billion tonnes. ... Returning temperatures towards 1.5C would require emissions cuts of 18% by 2030 and 69% by 2040, alongside large-scale carbon removal. The report warns those removal methods are costly and risky. Solar expansion has exceeded expectations but fossil fuels still supply most of the world’s energy. A New Mexico judge has ordered Meta to pay $25 billion for misleading Facebook users about control of their personal data. The ruling follows a jury finding that the company committed 43 million violations of state consumer protection law following the Cambridge Analytica scandal. Judge Francis Mathew said the deception was deliberate over years. ... The penalty, reduced from an initial calculation of $219 billion, is Meta’s largest to date. New Mexico will direct the award to a public education fund. Meta disputes the ruling and plans to appeal, arguing that the case seeks to impose restrictions on online speech.

items.title: Inflation worsened last month to 3.7% as midterm elections ...
items.excerpt: WASHINGTON (AP) — U.S. inflation accelerated last month as gas, clothes, and air fares got more expensive, evidence that rising prices remain an economic challenge just a few weeks before the midterm elections that have focused heavily on issues related to affordability. ... The consumer price index rose 3.7% in September compared with a year ago, the Labor Department said Wednesday, up from 3.4% in August. On a monthly basis, costs jumped 0.6% from August to September, the biggest gain in five months, up from a 0.4% increase the previous month. ... The figures underscore the lingering impact of the Iran war on gas prices and the stubborn persistence of inflation, which fell sharply from a 9.1% peak in 2022 but this year has ticked higher since the war began in late February. The rise isn't all linked to gas prices, as surging investment in data centers and AI has also pushed up prices for computer chips and the consumer electronics that also use them. Elevated inflation has posed political problems for Republicans in Congress and is a challenge for the Federal Reserve, which is required by Congress to seek stable prices. ... Excluding the volatile food and energy categories, core prices rose 2.6% in September from a year ago, up from 2.4% the previous month. And they climbed 0.3% from August to September, an elevated pace that, if it continued for a year, would run well above the Fed's 2% target. ... Federal Reserve officials are watching inflation data closely to determine whether they need to raise their short-term interest rate further, and by how much. ... Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh said last month that inflation isn't moving quickly enough back to the central bank's target, causing the Fed to hike rates for the first time in three years, to about 3.9%. ... Yet some key Fed officials have suggested the central bank can wait before increasing rates again. The Fed has a policy meeting Oct. 27-28, but most Wall Street investors expect it to hold rates then, and potentially implement another hike in December. Fed officials have penciled in just one more rate hike this year. ... By raising borrowing costs, the Fed hopes to slow spending and growth and cool price increases. Yet much of the current inflation comes from supply shocks, such as the Iran war's disruption to oil and gas supplies, and higher interest rates can't address those bottlenecks. ... Warsh has said his goal is to keep the gas price spike from seeping into more areas of the economy. It's already pushed up the price of air fares about 22% from a year ago. ... Gas prices jumped more than 9% from August to September, Wednesday's report said. Rising gas costs are a highly visible sign of inflation and often drive down measures of consumer sentiment about the economy. ... Prices at the pump have ticked lower in the past two weeks to a nationwide average of $4.33 a gallon, according to AAA, though they remain higher than a month ago. ... Those costs raise shipping and other expenses for many large and small businesses, some of which are forced to pass the cost to consumers. Last week, PepsiCo said that it will raise prices for its snack foods, including Doritos, Ruffles, Sun Chips, and some sodas to offset higher costs for fuel, aluminum, and food ingredients. ... The artificial intelligence buildout has also sharply elevated the cost of semiconductors, computer equipment, and electrical components, which have been passed on to consumers in the form of more expensive electronics such as gaming devices, laptops, and smartphones. Goldman Sachs estimated in a report Tuesday that the AI buildout has added about a half-percentage point to the annual inflation rate, according to the Fed's preferred inflation gauge.

items.title: Inflation Overshot Expectations in September | Fifth Third Bank
items.excerpt: Inflation surprised to the upside in September. Headline CPI matched expectations for the month, accelerating to 0.6% from 0.4% on a 9.1% jump in gasoline prices. The negative surprise was in core prices, which rose a faster-than-expected 0.3%. Price increases were widespread across the core CPI basket, affecting a range of durable goods, nondurables, and services. ... The PPI rose even more than the CPI, up 1.3% versus the 0.6% expected. Diesel surged a seasonally adjusted 21.0%. Producer prices for foods rose 1.2% on double-digit increases of fresh and dry vegetables, hay and hayseeds, grains, and oilseeds—rising prices of livestock feeds will likely translate to more expensive meat in 2027. Core PPI excluding food and energy rose 0.7% as trade services (Wholesale and retail margins) climbed 1.4% and energy-intensive transportation and warehousing charges jumped 3.4%. A silver lining is that many of the core PPI components that carry over into PCE inflation behaved better than the headline. These include portfolio management services, most medical services, and pharmaceuticals. ... Headlines were strong for the first September activity data, but the details were uneven. Retail sales rose a strong 0.8% on a 6.4% increase in gas station spending (All due to higher prices—recall gas prices jumped 9.1% in the CPI report). Other retail categories rose 0.2%, lagging the 0.3% increase of CPI core goods prices. Industrial production rose 0.7% as utilities output jumped 3.5%. This was the hottest September on record, boosting cooling demand. Manufacturing rose a more moderate 0.3% after declining 0.2% in August.

Ohio State University disputes DOJ finding that medical school discriminates in admissions Ohio State University said on Wednesday it disagreed with the US Department of Justice's findings that alleged its medical school favored Black and Hispanic applicants in admissions and discriminated against white and Asian applicants. Trump warns Kansans that US will 'burn' like France if Democrats win US ‌President Donald Trump on Monday used ​violent unrest in France as an argument against Democrats in his battle to defend a Kansas Senate seat long held by Republicans but in danger of falling to his political opponents. Trump's rally on behalf of Republican incumbent Roger Marshall was his latest foray into conservative states where Republican candidates are on defense due to voter frustrations over the Iran war and rising prices. New Mexico sues to stop payouts to Jeffrey Epstein's lawyer, accountant New Mexico has filed a civil lawsuit to block payments from Jeffrey Epstein's estate to the late sex offender's lawyer and accountant, and to recover damages for survivors of his alleged sexual abuse, the state's top law enforcement official said on Wednesday. The suit is the first law enforcement action against Epstein's longtime personal attorney Darren Indyke and accountant Richard Kahn, according to New Mexico Attorney General Raul Torrez. Trump to rally for Graham in tight South Carolina Senate race amid Russia rift President Donald Trump travels to South Carolina on Wednesday to bolster Republican Darline Graham in a surprisingly competitive Senate race, even as his recent moves toward Russia have put him at odds with the ‌sister of his late ally Lindsey Graham. Less than two weeks before the November 3 election, Darline Graham is running about even in the polls against Democrat Annie Andrews in a state Republicans typically win handily, another sign of the political headwinds confronting Trump's party amid high gasoline prices and the war in Iran. Trump administration says it has revoked over 300,000 visas President Donald Trump's administration has revoked over 300,000 US visas during his second term, the State Department said on Tuesday as the federal government continues its sweeping immigration crackdown. The number showed an acceleration in the pace of visa revocations in recent weeks. Vance defends Ramaswamy's explosive attack ad in Ohio governor race US Vice President JD Vance on Wednesday defended an explosive attack ad by Republican Vivek Ramaswamy’s campaign against his Democratic rival in the Ohio governor’s race. The ad features Democrat Amy Acton’s estranged mother, Donna Arthur, disputing Acton’s account of a childhood she says involved a period of homelessness and sexual abuse. Arthur, whom Acton says she has not seen since 1978, urges Ohioans not to vote for her daughter. Trump says fraud investigations make 'very big dent' in overseas scams President Donald Trump said on Wednesday his administration has made a "very big dent" in scams by foreign criminal networks that lure Americans into fraudulent investments, focusing on an anti-fraud message ahead of November's midterm elections. Trump, members of his cabinet and other top administration officials met at the White House for an event on cybercrime prevention, where FBI Director Kash Patel said his agency had taken down 20 scam compounds throughout the world. Lawmakers ‌say US briefing showed Russia targeting Democrats with misinformation The top Democratic lawmakers on the congressional intelligence committees on Wednesday said they received an intelligence briefing that Russia has been waging a misinformation campaign against Democrats running in next month's midterm elections. The comments by Senator Mark Warner and Representative Jim Himes come as Republican President Donald Trump has in recent weeks eased economic sanctions on Russia and increased pressure on Ukraine to end its fight against Russian forces. Supreme Court won't allow Trump administration restrictions on transgender inmates The US Supreme Court rejected on Wednesday a bid by President Donald Trump's administration to immediately enforce a policy restricting gender-affirming care for transgender inmates in federal prisons in a rare win for transgender rights at ‌the nation's top judicial body. The court denied the Justice Department's emergency request to lift a federal judge's order blocking the Federal Bureau of Prisons from implementing the policy, while a legal challenge to the measure plays out. items.title: Michael Jackson biopic loses Golden Globes musical bid
items.excerpt: The Michael Jackson biopic Michael is set to compete as a drama at next year's Golden Globe Awards after its bid to be considered a musical was rejected. Studio Lionsgate had submitted the blockbuster film, starring Jackson’s nephew Jaafar Jackson as the late King of Pop, for consideration in the musical or comedy categories. ... However, the Golden Globes awards committee turned down the request, meaning the film and its leading actor are now expected to compete in the drama categories. ... The committee reportedly determined that the performances in Michael, which recreate some of Jackson’s most famous songs and concerts, did not meet that requirement. ... If the ruling stands, Jaafar Jackson will compete for a nomination in the Best Actor in a Motion Picture - Drama category.

items.title: Telemundo Gears Up for Latin Music's Biggest Night: The 2026 Billboard Latin Music Awards to Air Live Thursday, October 22 - NBCUniversal Telemundo Enterprises Press Releases
items.excerpt: WHAT: Telemundo and Billboard announced the date for the 2026 Billboard Latin Music Awards, the longest-running and most prestigious awards show in Latin music. The live music special will bring fans together for an unforgettable celebration of Latin music’s biggest stars, honoring the year’s top artists, albums, and songs, while featuring exciting live performances from today’s top music talent. The Billboard Latin Music Awards is the only awards show to honor the most popular albums, songs, and performers in Latin music, as determined by the actual sales, streaming, radio airplay and social data that informs Billboard’s weekly charts during a one-year period. ... WHEN: Thursday, October 22 ... WHERE: The award show will take place at the James L. Knight Center in Miami, Florida, and will be available LIVE on Telemundo and Peacock. ... The awards will coincide with Billboard Latin Music Week, which returns to Miami October 19-22, celebrating Latin music, culture, and entertainment all week long with exclusive performances, one-of-a-kind conversations, workshops, showcases and exclusive fan experiences. Learn more about Billboard Latin Music Week at billboardlatinmusicweek.com.
